NB.name: Public Legal Education and Information Service of NB (PLEIS-NB)
NB.summary: Provides legal information to the public, including a toll-free Family Law Information Line and a toll-free Legal Information Line (French and English). General information, not individual legal advice.

NB.cat: If you're denied — legal help & appeals
NB.name: Legal Aid New Brunswick (NB Legal Aid Services Commission)
NB.summary: Helps people with low incomes with eligible criminal and family matters; duty counsel at courthouses is free for covered matters. PLEIS-NB's guide does not mention disability benefit appeals.
NB.urlText: Legal Aid in New Brunswick (PLEIS-NB guide)

NB.cat: If you're denied — legal help & appeals
NB.name: New Brunswick Human Rights Commission
NB.summary: Takes discrimination complaints on its approved forms, emailed to the Commission. Complaints can typically be filed for incidents within the last 12 months. You can call to ask about the process.

NB.name: Inclusion NB
NB.summary: Supports inclusion for people with disabilities and their families through Family Support, Inclusive Education, Inclusive Employment and Life in Community programs. Toll-free line; the inquiry form offers regions: Bathurst, Edmundston, Fredericton, Moncton, Miramichi, Saint John.

NB.name: 211 New Brunswick
NB.summary: The site identifies itself as 211 New Brunswick (a community services information service).

NB.name: Disability Alliance Canada
NB.summary: A national, cross-disability non-profit serving people with disabilities across Canada. Offers free one-on-one advocate support for CPP Disability and the Disability Tax Credit (DTC).

NB.name: Disability Planning Helpline (Plan Institute)
NB.summary: A free, nationwide (Canada-wide) helpline for disability planning questions, including the RDSP.

NB.name: Inclusion NB
NB.whatTheyDo: Supports inclusion for people with disabilities and their families through family support, inclusive education, inclusive employment and life-in-community programs, plus advocacy and training.

NB.name: Premier's Council on Disabilities
NB.whatTheyDo: A consultation, study and information-sharing body that advises the provincial government on issues affecting persons with disabilities and reports directly to the Premier (toll-free 1-800-442-4412).

NB.name: Easter Seals New Brunswick
NB.whatTheyDo: Has served people with disabilities since 1966. Programs listed include assistive technology, the accessible Camp Rotary and a Disability Travel Card, with pages on funding opportunities and the Disability Tax Credit.

NB.name: Autism Resource Centres of New Brunswick (regional network)
NB.whatTheyDo: Non-profit community centres offering free referrals, resources, support, education and outreach to people with ASD, their families and friends, and professionals.

NB.name: Public Legal Education and Information Service of NB (PLEIS-NB)
NB.whatTheyDo: Provides legal information to the public through toll-free information lines, free workshops and webinars, and a tenant information program.

NB.name: New Brunswick Human Rights Commission
NB.whatTheyDo: Receives human rights complaints on its approved forms; you can call (506) 453-2301 to ask about the process.
